mainTopic: The power of תפלה: רבי אלעזר's teachings, long and repeated prayer, ה׳ not forgetting Israel, and the משנה's rules on preparing for תפלה and not interrupting it.
overview: This amud is full of teachings about the power of תפלה. רבי אלעזר says תפלה is greater than good deeds and greater than קרבנות, and that a תענית is greater than צדקה. He also teaches that since the חורבן the gates of prayer are locked, but the gates of tears are still open. The גמרא praises long prayer and explains that it brings heartache only when a person expects an answer because he prayed long. Someone who was not answered should pray again, and a ברייתא lists four things that need constant strengthening: תורה, good deeds, תפלה and one's work. A midrash on ישעיהו shows ה׳ comforting ציון: He forgets the sin of the עגל but never forgets סיני. The גמרא then returns to the משנה, discussing the early חסידים who waited an hour before and after davening, and the rule not to stop even for a king's greeting. The amud ends with a story of a חסיד who ignored an officer's greeting, and his answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Prayer is greater than good deeds
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that תפלה is greater than מעשים טובים. Even משה רבינו, the greatest in good deeds, got an answer only through תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: Prayer is greater than good deeds. Nobody had more good deeds than משה רבינו, and still, he was answered only through prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר makes a bold claim: תפלה is greater than מעשים טובים. He supports it with the example of משה רבינו.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reasoning works like this: if good deeds alone could get a request answered, משה רבינו would surely have been answered because of them. Since even he was answered only when he davened, תפלה must have a power that good deeds alone do not have.

keyTerms.meaning: Is greater than. This is the comparison formula used in each of רבי אלעזר's teachings here.

steps.confusionAlert: רבי אלעזר is not saying good deeds don't matter. He means that good deeds alone, without תפלה, did not bring an answer, even for משה רבינו.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
Prayer is greater than good deeds,
for there is no one greater in good deeds
than Moshe our teacher,
and even so,
he was answered only through prayer.
phrases.notes: 'He' is משה, davening to be allowed into ארץ ישראל.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גְּדוֹלָה תְּפִלָּה יוֹתֵר מִמַּעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the section with the first of רבי אלעזר's comparisons.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפלה is greater than מעשים טובים, as shown by משה רבינו, who was answered only through תפלה.

steps.title: The verses showing משה was answered through prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא proves the point from two פסוקים that sit right next to each other. ה׳ says 'speak no more to Me,' and right after that tells משה to go up to the top of the mountain.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Do not speak to Me any more about this,' and right next to it: 'Go up to the top of the peak.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the source for רבי אלעזר's claim. It points to two פסוקים placed side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Speak no more to Me' shows that משה had been davening. Right next to it, ה׳ lets him climb up and see the land. Because the two פסוקים sit together, the partial answer came as a result of the תפלה.

keyTerms.meaning: As it says (introduces a פסוק as proof)
And right next to it is written
The top of the peak (the mountain where משה saw the land)

phrases.english: As it is said: 'Do not continue to speak to Me,'
phrases.notes: דברים 3:26

phrases.english: and right next to it: 'Go up to the top of the peak.'
phrases.notes: דברים 3:27. Right after his davening, משה is allowed to go up and see the land. That was the answer he got.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״אַל תּוֹסֶף דַּבֵּר אֵלַי״ וּסְמִיךְ לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק-based proof for the claim in step 1.
steps.raayaObject: That משה רבינו was answered only through תפלה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The two neighboring פסוקים in דברים 3:26-27: 'speak no more to Me' and 'go up to the top of the peak.'

steps.title: Fasting is greater than charity
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר gives a second comparison: תענית is greater than צדקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר also said: A fast is greater than charity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching from רבי אלעזר in the same style: one מצוה is 'greater' than another. This time it is תענית compared to צדקה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word 'וְאָמַר' (and he also said) tells us we are in a series of teachings from the same רבי אלעזר. Here he only states the claim; the reason comes in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: And he also said (marks another teaching from the same רבי)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
A fast is greater than charity.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גְּדוֹלָה תַּעֲנִית יוֹתֵר מִן הַצְּדָקָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new, separate comparison by the same רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תענית is greater than צדקה.

steps.title: Asking for the reason
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why fasting should count as greater than charity.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the logic behind רבי אלעזר's claim. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unlike the first teaching, no פסוק was given here. So the גמרא wants to know what reasoning makes תענית greater than צדקה.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind step 3.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why תענית is greater than צדקה.

steps.title: Body versus money
steps.stepSummary: A fast is done with your own body, while צדקה is done only with your money.
steps.simpleTranslation: This one is with his body, and that one is with his money.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. A תענית is greater because it is done with your body, while צדקה is done with your money.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When you fast, you afflict yourself and give up something from your own body. צדקה costs money, which is outside of you. A מצוה that uses your very self is considered greater.
steps.whatToRemember: תענית is greater than צדקה because a fast uses the person's body, while צדקה uses only his money.

phrases.english: This one is with his body, and that one is with his money.
phrases.notes: 'This one' is the fast and 'that one' is the צדקה.

steps.triggerLanguage: זֶה בְּגוּפוֹ, וְזֶה בְּמָמוֹנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A תענית is done with one's body, while צדקה is done only with one's money, so the תענית is greater.

steps.title: Prayer is greater than sacrifices
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר's third comparison: תפלה is greater than קרבנות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Prayer is greater than sacrifices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a third teaching of רבי אלעזר. This time תפלה is compared to קרבנות, and the proof comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a different comparison from step 1. There, תפלה was compared to good deeds. Here it is compared to bringing קרבנות in the בית המקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacrifices (offerings brought in the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
Prayer is greater than sacrifices,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: גְּדוֹלָה תְּפִלָּה יוֹתֵר מִן הַקָּרְבָּנוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A third, separate comparison by רבי אלעזר.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תפלה is greater than קרבנות.

steps.title: Proof from the order of verses in ישעיהו
steps.stepSummary: ישעיהו first says ה׳ doesn't want their many קרבנות. Later he says ה׳ won't even accept their spread-out hands in תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'What need do I have for your many sacrifices,' and it is written: 'And when you spread out your hands.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא proves רבי אלעזר's point from two פסוקים in ישעיהו chapter 1.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The נביא builds up his rebuke step by step. First he says ה׳ rejects their קרבנות. Then he adds that even their תפלה, when they spread their hands, will not be accepted. Rejecting תפלה is the stronger statement, which shows that תפלה is on a higher level than קרבנות.

keyTerms.meaning: And it is written (introduces another פסוק)
And when you spread out your hands (in prayer)

steps.whatToRemember: תפלה is greater than קרבנות, because ישעיהו mentions it after קרבנות as the bigger thing ה׳ would refuse.

phrases.english: As it is said: 'Why do I need your many sacrifices,'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:11

phrases.english: and it is written: 'And when you spread out your hands.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:15. That פסוק goes on: even if you pray a lot, I won't listen. So now even their תפלה is turned away.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר ״לָמָּה לִּי רֹב זִבְחֵיכֶם״, וּכְתִיב: ״וּבְפָרִשְׂכֶם כַּפֵּיכֶם״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק-based proof for the claim in step 6.
steps.raayaObject: That תפלה is greater than קרבנות.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 1:11 and 1:15. The rejection of קרבנות is followed by the stronger rejection of תפלה.

steps.title: A priest who killed may not bless the people
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן rules that a כהן who killed a person may not say ברכת כהנים. He learns this from the same פסוק in ישעיהו: 'your hands are full of blood.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Any priest who killed a person may not lift his hands to bless the people, as it says: 'Your hands are full of blood.'
steps.whatsHappening: Since the גמרא just quoted 'when you spread out your hands' from ישעיהו, it brings a halacha of רבי יוחנן based on the end of that same פסוק. A כהן who killed someone does not say ברכת כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: כהנים spread out their hands when they say ברכת כהנים. The פסוק says ה׳ turns away from hands spread out when those hands are 'full of blood.' So a כהן who killed a person may not lift his hands to bless.

keyTerms.meaning: A priest, a descendant of אהרן
Lift his hands, meaning say ברכת כהנים
Your hands are full of blood

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a practical halacha that comes up in the laws of ברכת כהנים: a כהן who killed someone is not allowed to bless the people.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Any priest who killed a person
may not lift his hands,
phrases.notes: 'Lifting his hands' means saying ברכת כהנים, when the כהנים raise their hands to bless the people.

phrases.english: as it is said: 'Your hands are full of blood.'
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:15. These are the closing words of the same פסוק that starts 'when you spread out your hands.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל כֹּהֵן שֶׁהָרַג אֶת הַנֶּפֶשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the פסוק quoted in step 7 to bring a related halacha from a different אמורא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן who killed a person may not say ברכת כהנים, based on 'your hands are full of blood.'

steps.title: Since the Temple was destroyed, the gates of prayer are locked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that since the חורבן, the gates of תפלה have been locked, and brings a פסוק from איכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר also said: Since the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, the gates of prayer have been locked, as it says: 'Even when I cry out and plead, He shuts out my prayer.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another teaching of רבי אלעזר about תפלה. He says that since the חורבן, prayer is not accepted the way it used to be.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof comes from איכה, which was written about the חורבן. In that פסוק, the speaker cries out and still feels his prayer is shut out. רבי אלעזר reads this as describing how things have been ever since the destruction.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
From the day the Temple was destroyed
the gates of prayer were locked,
as it says: "Even when I cry out and plead,
He shuts out my prayer."
phrases.notes: איכה 3:8

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the series of statements about תפלה, now turning to how the חורבן changed prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, the gates of תפלה are locked.

steps.title: But the gates of tears are never locked
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר adds that even though the gates of prayer are locked, the gates of tears are still open, and proves it from תהלים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And even though the gates of prayer were locked, the gates of tears were not locked, as it says: 'Hear my prayer, ה׳, and listen to my cry; do not be silent to my tears.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר softens what he just said. A prayer said with tears still gets through.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new idea is that one kind of prayer is still open: prayer with tears. In the פסוק, דוד המלך asks ה׳ not to be silent to his tears. That shows tears get a special hearing.
steps.whatToRemember: After the חורבן, ordinary prayer has a harder time getting through, but a prayer with real tears is always heard.

phrases.aramaic: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשַּׁעֲרֵי תְפִילָּה נִנְעֲלוּ,
phrases.english: And even though the gates of prayer were locked,
the gates of tears were not locked,
as it says: "Hear my prayer, ה׳,
and listen to my cry;
do not be silent to my tears."
phrases.notes: תהלים 39:13

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאַף עַל פִּי שֶׁשַּׁעֲרֵי תְפִילָּה נִנְעֲלוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds an exception to step 9: tears still get through the locked gates.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Prayer with tears is still accepted, even after the חורבן.

steps.title: רבא would not declare a fast on a cloudy day
steps.stepSummary: רבא's practice was not to declare a public fast on a cloudy day, because a פסוק says a cloud blocks prayer.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא would not declare a fast on a cloudy day, because it says: 'You covered Yourself with a cloud, so that prayer cannot pass through.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells us what רבא actually did. This is connected to the idea that prayer can be blocked.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A fast day is a day of extra prayer. The פסוק in איכה describes a cloud that keeps prayer from passing through. So רבא saw a cloudy day as a bad time to call a fast.

phrases.english: Rava would not declare a fast
on a cloudy day,
because it says:
"You covered Yourself with a cloud
so that prayer cannot pass through."
phrases.notes: איכה 3:44

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבָא לָא גְּזַר תַּעֲנִיתָא בְּיוֹמָא דְעֵיבָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows a real-life practice based on the idea from step 9 that prayer can be blocked.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not declare a public fast on a cloudy day, since a cloud is a sign that prayer is being blocked.

steps.title: Since the Temple was destroyed, an iron wall separates us from ה׳
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר says that since the חורבן, an iron wall has stood between ישראל and their Father in heaven, and proves it from יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אלעזר said: Since the day the בית המקדש was destroyed, an iron wall has separated ישראל from their Father in heaven, as it says: 'And you, take for yourself an iron pan, and set it up as an iron wall between you and the city.'
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר gives one more picture of what the חורבן did. There is now something like a wall between us and ה׳.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ told the נביא יחזקאל to put up an iron pan as a wall between himself and the city. רבי אלעזר reads this as a sign of the separation between ישראל and ה׳ since the חורבן.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't read נִפְסְקָה as 'stopped' or 'was removed.' Here it means the iron wall came in between ישראל and ה׳.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Elazar said:
From the day the Temple was destroyed
an iron wall has separated
between Israel and their Father in heaven,
as it says: "And you, take for yourself an iron pan,
and set it up as an iron wall
between you and the city."
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 4:3

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מִיּוֹם שֶׁחָרַב בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ נִפְסְקָה חוֹמַת בַּרְזֶל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second teaching of רבי אלעזר about the effect of the חורבן, parallel to step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Since the חורבן, an iron wall separates ישראל from ה׳.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי אלעזר gives two pictures of the חורבן: locked gates of prayer (except for tears) and an iron wall between us and ה׳.

steps.title: A long prayer never comes back empty
steps.stepSummary: רבי חנין, in the name of רבי חנינא, says that whoever makes his prayer long will not have it come back unanswered.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חנין said in the name of רבי חנינא: Anyone who makes his prayer long, his prayer does not come back empty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new, encouraging statement about תפלה. The next step will ask where this comes from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The steps before this were about prayer being blocked. This statement gives a hopeful message: putting in a long, drawn-out effort in prayer brings results.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנִין אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Chanin said in the name of Rabbi Chanina:
Anyone who makes his prayer long,
his prayer does not come back empty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָנִין אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא: כׇּל הַמַּאֲרִיךְ בִּתְפִלָּתוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the blocking of prayer to a new, positive teaching about long prayer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A long prayer is not turned away unanswered.

steps.title: Where do we learn this?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a long prayer is answered.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for רבי חנינא's statement. It is setting up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not an attack on the statement. It is a simple request: show us where in the תורה we see that a long prayer gets answered.

phrases.english: From where do we know this?

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא לַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the statement in step 13.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural source that a long prayer does not return unanswered.

steps.title: The proof from משה רבינו's long prayer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from משה רבינו: he prayed at length, and right after that the פסוק says ה׳ listened to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: From משה רבינו, as it says: 'And I prayed to ה׳,' and it is written after it: 'And ה׳ listened to me that time too.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question with משה רבינו. He prayed a long time, and ה׳ answered him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: משה's prayer after the חטא העגל lasted forty days and nights, so it was a long prayer. The פסוקים that come soon after say ה׳ listened to him. That shows a long prayer is answered.
steps.whatToRemember: Long, persistent prayer works. We learn it from משה רבינו, whose forty-day prayer was answered.

phrases.english: From Moshe our teacher,
as it says: "And I prayed to ה׳,"
phrases.notes: דברים 9:26. This prayer lasted forty days and nights, which is what makes it a long prayer.

phrases.english: and it is written after it:
"And ה׳ listened to me that time too."
phrases.notes: דברים 10:10

steps.triggerLanguage: מִמֹּשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״וָאֶתְפַּלֵּל אֶל ה׳״
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: משה prayed a long prayer, and the פסוק right after says ה׳ listened, which proves a long prayer is answered.
steps.raayaObject: רבי חנינא's statement that a long prayer does not return empty

steps.title: Long prayer can lead to heartache
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רבי חנין's praise of long prayer with רבי יוחנן's statement that a long prayer, when a person expects an answer, leads to heartache.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? רבי חייא בר אבא said in the name of רבי יוחנן: anyone who prays at length and expects an answer will end up with heartache, as the פסוק says, 'Hope that drags on makes the heart sick.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks what we just learned in steps 13 to 15, that a long prayer is a good thing. It brings רבי יוחנן, who says a long prayer can end in heartache.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי חנין said a long prayer will not come back empty. רבי יוחנן says a long prayer, with expectation, leads to a sick heart when the answer does not come. These two statements seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: Is that so? An opening word for a challenge
One who makes his prayer long
He expects it to be answered

phrases.english: Is that so?!

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Chiyya bar Abba say
that Rabbi Yochanan said:
Anyone who makes his prayer long
and expects it to be answered
phrases.notes: Literally 'looks into it.'

phrases.english: will end up with heartache,
as it says: 'Hope that drags on makes the heart sick.'
phrases.notes: משלי 13:12

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי?! וְהָא אָמַר רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the teaching of steps 13 to 15 that a long prayer is answered.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי חנין's statement that one who prays at length will not have his prayer come back empty.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says long prayer leads to heartache, which seems to be the opposite of praising it.

steps.title: The fix for heartache is learning Torah
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's statement continues: the cure for this heartache is to learn תורה, which is called a 'tree of life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: What is his fix? He should learn תורה, as it says, 'But a wish that comes true is a tree of life,' and 'tree of life' means only תורה, as it says, 'It is a tree of life to those who hold on to it.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is still part of רבי יוחנן's statement. After describing the heartache, he gives the cure: learning תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second half of the same פסוק in משלי says a wish that comes true is a 'tree of life.' Another פסוק calls תורה a 'tree of life.' So the cure for a sick heart is תורה. This is a side point and does not change the challenge.

keyTerms.meaning: He should busy himself with תורה
To those who hold on to it

phrases.english: What is his fix?
He should busy himself with Torah,
as it says: 'But a wish that comes true is a tree of life,'
phrases.notes: This is the second half of the same פסוק, משלי 13:12.

phrases.english: and 'tree of life' means only Torah,
as it says: 'It is a tree of life
to those who hold on to it.'
phrases.notes: משלי 3:18

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי תַּקַּנְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the quote from רבי יוחנן brought in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone suffering heartache from unanswered prayer should learn תורה, which is a 'tree of life.'

steps.title: Expecting an answer versus not expecting one
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction: רבי יוחנן speaks about someone who prays long and expects an answer, and רבי חנין speaks about someone who prays long without expecting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is not difficult. This one is about someone who prays long and expects an answer; that one is about someone who prays long and does not expect an answer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from step 16 by showing that the two statements describe two different kinds of people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Praying long is good. What brings heartache is praying long while counting on the length to force an answer. If a person prays long without that expectation, רבי חנין's promise applies.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult; the two sources do not clash
This one ... that one; each source has its own case

steps.whatToRemember: Long prayer is praised. The heartache comes only when a person expects an answer because he prayed long.
steps.confusionAlert: The text does not say which 'הָא' goes with which source. The first (expects an answer) is רבי יוחנן's heartache case, and the second (does not expect) is רבי חנין's praised case.

phrases.english: It is not difficult:
this one is where he prays long and expects an answer;
phrases.notes: This is רבי יוחנן's case, the one that leads to heartache.

phrases.english: that one is where he prays long and does not expect an answer.
phrases.notes: This is רבי חנין's case from step 13, the one that gets answered.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּמַאֲרֵיךְ וּמְעַיֵּין בַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge raised in step 16.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the cases: the two statements apply to two different attitudes in prayer.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It seemed that רבי חנין praises long prayer and רבי יוחנן criticizes it.
steps.terutzMaskana: Long prayer without expecting an answer is praised. Long prayer while expecting an answer leads to heartache.

steps.title: If not answered, pray again
steps.stepSummary: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא teaches that a person who prayed and was not answered should pray again, based on a פסוק that says 'hope to ה׳' twice.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חמא ברבי חנינא said: if a person sees that he prayed and was not answered, he should pray again, as it says, 'Hope to ה׳, be strong and let your heart be brave, and hope to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching on a related idea: what to do when a prayer was not answered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says 'hope to ה׳' twice. The second time teaches that if the first hope was not answered, a person should turn to ה׳ in prayer again. Not being answered is not a reason to stop praying.

keyTerms.meaning: He should go back and pray again

phrases.english: Rabbi Chama son of Rabbi Chanina said:
If a person sees that he prayed
and was not answered
he should go back and pray again,
as it says: 'Hope to ה׳,
be strong and let your heart be brave,
and hope to ה׳.'
phrases.notes: תהלים 27:14. Notice 'hope to ה׳' comes twice: hope, and if needed, hope again.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי חָמָא בְּרַבִּי חֲנִינָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on a related theme, what to do when prayer is not answered.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone whose prayer was not answered should pray again.

steps.title: Four things need strengthening
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that four things need constant strengthening: תורה, מעשים טובים, תפלה, and דרך ארץ.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: four things need strengthening, and these are: תורה, good deeds, prayer, and earning a living.
steps.whatsHappening: Since the last פסוק said 'be strong' about prayer, the גמרא brings a ברייתא listing four things that need strengthening. This sets up the next steps, where each item gets a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These four areas need ongoing effort, not just a one-time push. The list is stated here, and the proofs come next.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: one's work, earning a living

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
Four things need strengthening,
and these are they:
Torah, and good deeds,
prayer, and earning a living.
phrases.notes: דרך ארץ here doesn't mean manners. It means a person's work or job.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אַרְבָּעָה צְרִיכִין חִזּוּק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the word 'be strong' in the פסוק of step 19 and widens it to four areas.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: תורה, מעשים טובים, תפלה, and דרך ארץ all need constant strengthening.

steps.title: Asking for the source for Torah and good deeds
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks where we learn that תורה and מעשים טובים need strengthening.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know that תורה and good deeds need strengthening?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts proving the ברייתא's list one item at a time. First it asks for the source for תורה and good deeds, setting up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא stated four items without proof. The גמרא wants a פסוק behind each, and it groups the first two together because one פסוק covers both.

phrases.english: From where do we know Torah and good deeds?

steps.triggerLanguage: תּוֹרָה וּמַעֲשִׂים טוֹבִים מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the first two items on the ברייתא's list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that תורה and מעשים טובים need strengthening.

steps.title: Be strong in תורה, brave in good deeds
steps.stepSummary: The answer comes from the פסוק told to יהושע: 'be strong' refers to תורה and 'be brave' refers to מעשים טובים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it says: 'Only be strong and very brave to guard and to do according to all the תורה.' 'Be strong' means in תורה, and 'be brave' means in good deeds.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 21 with a פסוק from ספר יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses two words, 'strong' and 'brave.' The גמרא reads them as two separate things: strength in learning תורה and courage in doing good deeds. So both items need strengthening.

phrases.english: As it says: 'Only be strong and very brave
to guard and to do according to all the Torah,'
phrases.notes: יהושע 1:7

phrases.english: 'Be strong' — in Torah,
'and brave' — in good deeds.

steps.triggerLanguage: שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר: ״רַק חֲזַק וֶאֱמַץ מְאֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 21.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק in יהושע says 'be strong and brave'. 'Strong' is about תורה, and 'brave' is about מעשים טובים.

steps.title: The Source That Prayer Needs Strengthening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from תהלים showing that תפלה needs strengthening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that prayer needs strengthening? From the פסוק: 'Hope to ה׳, be strong and let your heart be brave, and hope to ה׳.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the third item on the ברייתא's list. It asks where we learn that תפלה needs strengthening and answers right away with a פסוק from תהלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts 'be strong' right next to 'hope to ה׳,' which is prayer. Because 'hope to ה׳' appears twice, it also fits with step 19: if you prayed and were not answered, pray again.

keyTerms.meaning: Hope to ה׳, meaning turn to Him in prayer

phrases.english: Prayer, from where do we know it needs strengthening?
As it says: 'Hope to ה׳,
phrases.notes: תהלים 27:14

phrases.english: be strong and let your heart be brave,
and hope to ה׳.'

steps.triggerLanguage: תְּפִלָּה מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of sources: after תורה and מעשים טובים, now תפלה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that תפלה needs strengthening.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'קוה אל ה׳ חזק ויאמץ לבך וקוה אל ה׳' links strengthening to prayer.

steps.title: The Source That One's Work Needs Strengthening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a פסוק from שמואל showing that דרך ארץ needs strengthening.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we learn that דרך ארץ (a person's work and everyday activity) needs strengthening? From the פסוק: 'Be strong and let us strengthen ourselves for our people.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the last of the four sources, the one for דרך ארץ.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the פסוק, יואב tells his brother אבישי before a battle to be strong for the sake of the people. The גמרא uses this call to be strong in a worldly task to show that a person's everyday work also needs effort and strength.

keyTerms.meaning: Here: one's occupation and worldly activity
Be strong and let us strengthen ourselves

steps.whatToRemember: All four from the ברייתא now have a source: תורה and מעשים טובים from יהושע, תפלה from תהלים, and דרך ארץ from שמואל.

phrases.english: Worldly occupation, from where do we know it needs strengthening?
As it says: 'Be strong and let us strengthen ourselves
phrases.notes: שמואל ב 10:12

phrases.english: for the sake of our people, etc.'

steps.triggerLanguage: דֶּרֶךְ אֶרֶץ מִנַּיִן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the list of four sources begun in step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that דרך ארץ needs strengthening.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק 'חזק ונתחזק בעד עמנו' shows strengthening in worldly tasks.

steps.title: Why Does the Verse Say Both 'Left' and 'Forgotten'?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק where ציון says ה׳ left and forgot her, and asks why both words are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says: 'ציון said, ה׳ has left me, and ה׳ has forgotten me.' Isn't 'left' the same as 'forgotten'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a פסוק from ישעיהו and asks why it seems to say the same thing twice. This sets up ריש לקיש's explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumes the תורה doesn't waste words. If 'left' and 'forgotten' mean the same thing, one of them seems extra, so the גמרא wants to know what each word adds.

keyTerms.meaning: ציון, standing for the Jewish people

phrases.english: 'And ציון said: Hashem has left me,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:14

phrases.english: and ה׳ has forgotten me.'
Isn't 'left' the same as 'forgotten'?

steps.triggerLanguage: הַיְינוּ עֲזוּבָה, הַיְינוּ שְׁכוּחָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic. The ברייתא's list is finished, and the גמרא moves to a new aggadic פסוק.
steps.kashyaTarget: The double wording 'עזבני' and 'שכחני' in ישעיהו 49:14.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two words that mean the same thing would make one of them extra.

steps.title: Being Forgotten Is Worse Than Being Left
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains that כנסת ישראל complained that ה׳ not only left her but also forgot her, which is worse than how a man treats a first wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: כנסת ישראל said to ה׳: Master of the world, even when a man marries a second wife after his first one, he still remembers what the first one did. But You have left me and also forgotten me.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question by showing that 'left' and 'forgotten' are two different levels of hurt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who takes another wife has in some way moved on from the first, but he still remembers her good deeds. כנסת ישראל says ה׳ did both: He moved on ('left') and also forgot what she did ('forgot'). So each word adds something.

keyTerms.meaning: The Jewish people as one community

steps.confusionAlert: This is a complaint that כנסת ישראל makes. It is not the גמרא's conclusion that ה׳ really forgot. The next step shows ה׳ rejecting the complaint.

phrases.english: ריש לקיש said:
The community of Israel said
before the Holy One, Blessed is He:
Master of the world,

phrases.aramaic: אָדָם נוֹשֵׂא אִשָּׁה עַל אִשְׁתּוֹ רִאשׁוֹנָה,
phrases.english: a man marries a wife in addition to his first wife,
yet he remembers the deeds of the first one.
But You have left me and forgotten me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: אָמְרָה כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל לִפְנֵי הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 25 by giving each word its own meaning.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the two words: 'left' means moving on, and 'forgotten' means no longer remembering past deeds.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: עזבני and שכחני seemed to mean the same thing.
steps.terutzMaskana: שכחני adds that even the memory of Israel's past deeds is gone, which is worse than just being left.

steps.title: ה׳ Answers: I Created the Whole Heavens for You
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ tells כנסת ישראל that He created a huge, layered army of heavenly bodies only for her sake, so she cannot say He forgot her.
steps.simpleTranslation: ה׳ said to her: My daughter, I created twelve constellations in the sky. For each one I created thirty armies, for each army thirty legions, for each legion thirty divisions, for each division thirty camps, and for each camp thirty forts. On each fort I hung 365 thousand myriads of stars, matching the days of the solar year. I created all of them only for you, and you say 'You left me' and 'You forgot me'?!
steps.whatsHappening: The midrash continues with ה׳'s reply, which rejects כנסת ישראל's complaint.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ה׳ describes a huge chain of creation: each level is multiplied by thirty, and then countless stars are hung on the last level. The point is that everything in the heavens exists only for Israel's sake, so it makes no sense to say ה׳ forgot her.
steps.whatToRemember: Israel felt both left and forgotten, but ה׳ answers that the whole universe was made only for her. She is never forgotten.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed is He, said to her:

phrases.aramaic: בִּתִּי, שְׁנֵים עָשָׂר מַזָּלוֹת בָּרָאתִי בָּרָקִיעַ,
phrases.english: My daughter, I created twelve constellations in the sky,
and for each and every constellation
I created thirty armies,
and for each and every army
I created thirty legions,
and for each and every legion
I created thirty divisions,
phrases.notes: These are army ranks, each one smaller than the one before.

phrases.english: and for each and every division
I created thirty camps,
and for each and every camp
I created thirty forts,
and on each and every fort

phrases.aramaic: תָּלִיתִי בּוֹ שְׁלֹשׁ מֵאוֹת וְשִׁשִּׁים וַחֲמִשָּׁה
phrases.english: I hung three hundred and sixty-five
thousand myriads of stars,
phrases.notes: A רבוא is ten thousand.

phrases.english: matching the days of the solar year.
And I created all of them only for your sake,
and you say 'You left me' and 'You forgot me'?!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: בִּתִּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ריש לקיש's midrash: ה׳ answers and rejects כנסת ישראל's complaint from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: All of creation, down to every star, exists for Israel's sake, so Israel is not forgotten.

steps.title: ה׳ has not forgotten Israel's offerings
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ reads the word עולה in the פסוק as a hint to the עולות Israel brought in the מדבר, and says He has not forgotten them.
steps.simpleTranslation: The פסוק says "Can a woman forget her baby?" ה׳ says: Would I ever forget the ram offerings and firstborn animals you brought Me in the desert?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps reading the פסוק in ישעיהו as ה׳'s reply to ציון's complaint. ה׳ says He remembers the קרבנות Israel brought in the מדבר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word עוּלָהּ (her baby) sounds like עוֹלוֹת (burnt offerings), so it is read as a hint to Israel's קרבנות. This adds a second comfort to step 27. ה׳ not only made the stars for Israel's sake, He also remembers what Israel did for Him.

keyTerms.meaning: her nursing baby; here read as a hint to עוֹלוֹת
firstborn animals (literally, those that open the womb)
would I ever? (a question that expects "no")

phrases.english: "Can a woman forget her nursing baby?"
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 49:15. The word עוּלָהּ is being read like עוֹלוֹת, burnt offerings.

phrases.english: The Holy One, Blessed be He, said:
Would I ever forget the burnt offerings of rams
and the firstborn animals
that you offered before Me in the desert?!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲתִשְׁכַּח אִשָּׁה עוּלָהּ אָמַר הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues ה׳'s reply to ציון's complaint from step 27, using the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ה׳ does not forget the קרבנות Israel brought in the מדבר.

steps.title: If ה׳ never forgets, what about the Golden Calf?
steps.stepSummary: כנסת ישראל turns ה׳'s words around: if nothing is forgotten before Him, then the sin of the עגל will not be forgotten either.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: Master of the World, since nothing is forgotten before You, maybe You will also never forget the sin of the Calf?
steps.whatsHappening: כנסת ישראל raises a worry about ה׳'s promise to remember everything. This sets up ה׳'s answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Being remembered is good for the קרבנות but bad for the sins. If ה׳ forgets nothing, the עגל should be remembered too. The comfort in step 28 seems to work against Israel.

keyTerms.meaning: the sin of the Golden Calf

phrases.english: She said before Him:
phrases.notes: "She" is כנסת ישראל, the people of Israel as a whole.

phrases.english: Master of the World,
since there is no forgetting
before Your Throne of Glory,

phrases.aramaic: שֶׁמָּא לֹא תִּשְׁכַּח לִי מַעֲשֵׂה הָעֵגֶל?
phrases.english: perhaps You will not forget my sin of the Calf?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְאֵין שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the comfort of step 28 by drawing out a bad result from it.
steps.kashyaTarget: ה׳'s statement that He forgets nothing (step 28).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If nothing is forgotten, Israel's sins, such as the עגל, must also be remembered.

steps.title: The Calf will be forgotten
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers with the פסוק: "These too shall be forgotten." The עגל will be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: "These too shall be forgotten."
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers Israel's worry about the עגל. He uses the next words of the פסוק to say that the עגל will be forgotten.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אֵלֶּה (these) hints at the עגל, since that is the word Israel used at the time of the sin. So ה׳ chooses to forget the sin while still remembering the good.

phrases.english: He said to her:
"These too shall be forgotten."
phrases.notes: "These" hints at the עגל, where they said "אֵלֶּה אֱלֹהֶיךָ", "these are your gods."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ גַּם אֵלֶּה תִשְׁכַּחְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 29.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the next words of the פסוק as being about the עגל.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: ה׳'s perfect memory means the עגל is remembered forever.
steps.terutzMaskana: ה׳ lets the sin of the עגל be forgotten.

steps.title: If ה׳ can forget, what about סיני?
steps.stepSummary: כנסת ישראל now worries the other way: if there is forgetting before ה׳, maybe מעמד הר סיני will be forgotten too.
steps.simpleTranslation: She said: Master of the World, since there is forgetting before You, maybe You will forget the events of סיני?
steps.whatsHappening: כנסת ישראל raises the opposite worry. ה׳'s answer comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once ה׳ has said that some things are forgotten, Israel fears that their greatest merit, accepting the תורה at סיני, could be forgotten too. Each answer seems to bring a new problem.

keyTerms.meaning: the events at הר סיני, when Israel received the תורה

phrases.english: She said before Him:
Master of the World,
since there is forgetting
before Your Throne of Glory,
perhaps You will forget the events of Sinai for me?

steps.triggerLanguage: הוֹאִיל וְיֵשׁ שִׁכְחָה לִפְנֵי כִּסֵּא כְבוֹדֶךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns step 30's answer around: if forgetting exists, it could hurt Israel.
steps.kashyaTarget: ה׳'s answer that the עגל will be forgotten (step 30).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If ה׳ can forget, then Israel's merit at סיני could also be forgotten.

steps.title: סיני will never be forgotten
steps.stepSummary: ה׳ answers with the end of the פסוק: "But I will not forget you." סיני will never be forgotten.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to her: "But I [אָנֹכִי] will not forget you."
steps.whatsHappening: ה׳ answers the second worry. Using the end of the פסוק, He promises never to forget סיני.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אָנֹכִי hints at סיני, because the עשרת הדברות begin with "אָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ". So the one פסוק holds both answers: the sin is forgotten, and the merit stays forever.

keyTerms.meaning: but I will not forget you

steps.whatToRemember: ה׳ forgets Israel's sin (the עגל) but never forgets their merit (סיני). Both come from the same פסוק.

phrases.english: He said to her:
"But I will not forget you."
phrases.notes: אָנֹכִי recalls "אָנֹכִי ה׳ אֱלֹהֶיךָ", the first of the עשרת הדברות at סיני.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָהּ וְאָנֹכִי לֹא אֶשְׁכָּחֵךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the worry of step 31.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reads the end of the פסוק as being about סיני.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If ה׳ forgets, סיני might be forgotten too.
steps.terutzMaskana: סיני is never forgotten, even though the עגל is.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's teaching supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא shows that this reading matches what רבי אלעזר taught in the name of רב אושעיא: "these" is the עגל, and "I" is סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what רבי אלעזר said in the name of רב אושעיא: "These too shall be forgotten" refers to the עגל, and "But I will not forget you" refers to סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the explanation it just gave by quoting an אמורא who said the same thing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase "והיינו" (and this is) tells us the story above matches a known teaching. רב אושעיא ties each half of the פסוק to a specific event, which supports steps 30 and 32.

keyTerms.meaning: what is meant by what is written

phrases.english: And this is what Rabbi Elazar said
that Rav Oshaya said:
What is meant by what is written, "These too shall be forgotten"?
This is the sin of the Calf.
"But I will not forget you"
this is the events of Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דְּאָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַב אוֹשַׁעְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the readings given in steps 30 and 32.
steps.raayaObject: Reading "גם אלה" as the עגל and "אנכי" as סיני.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רבי אלעזר in the name of רב אושעיא.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: the early pious ones waited an hour
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה, which says the early חסידים would wait one hour before davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: The early pious ones would wait one hour.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה. This sets up a new discussion explaining it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The long side discussion about תפלה and ה׳ not forgetting Israel is over. The גמרא now goes back to the משנה's words, about the early חסידים waiting before תפלה to get into the right frame of mind.
steps.confusionAlert: This line does not continue רב אושעיא's teaching. It is a new quote from the משנה, which the גמרא is about to explain.

phrases.english: The early pious ones
phrases.notes: This is a quote from the משנה at the start of the פרק; the גמרא now comes back to explain it.

phrases.english: would wait one hour.

steps.triggerLanguage: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִין שָׁעָה אַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the side discussion and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The early חסידים waited one hour before davening.

steps.title: Where does the rule of waiting before davening come from?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the משנה's practice of waiting one hour before davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: From where do we know these things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for a source for what the משנה just said: that the early חסידים waited an hour before davening. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה described a practice but gave no source. The גמרא wants to know what in the תורה or נביאים supports it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know these things? (asking for a source)

phrases.english: From where are these matters derived?
phrases.notes: "These matters" means the משנה's practice of waiting an hour before davening.

steps.triggerLanguage: מְנָא הָנֵי מִילֵּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the משנה quoted in step 34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: A פסוק that supports waiting before תפלה.

steps.title: The source: those who sit in Your House
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי brings the פסוק "Happy are those who dwell in Your House" as the source for waiting before davening.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע בן לוי said: The פסוק says, "Happy are those who dwell in Your House."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי answers with a פסוק from תהלים that praises people who sit in ה׳'s house.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first talks about sitting in ה׳'s house, and only after that about praising Him. So first you sit and wait, and then you daven.

keyTerms.meaning: Happy are those who dwell in Your House

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
The verse says: "Happy are those who dwell in Your House."
phrases.notes: תהלים 84:5. The next words are "they will yet praise You," so the sitting comes before the praising.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי, אָמַר קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 35.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק "אשרי יושבי ביתך" shows that one sits in ה׳'s house before praising Him.

steps.title: Waiting one hour after davening too
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע בן לוי adds that a person should also wait one hour after davening, based on a פסוק about the upright sitting before ה׳.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יהושע בן לוי said: One who davens must wait one hour after his תפלה, as it says: "Surely the righteous will give thanks to Your name; the upright will sit before You."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע בן לוי teaches a second rule: wait one hour after davening as well, and he brings a different פסוק for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה only spoke about waiting before davening. Here we learn a new rule about waiting afterward. In the פסוק, giving thanks (davening) comes first and sitting before ה׳ comes after.

keyTerms.meaning: The upright will sit before You

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi said:
One who prays must wait
one hour after his prayer,
as it is stated: "Surely the righteous will give thanks to Your name,
phrases.notes: תהלים 140:14

phrases.english: the upright will sit before You."

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ בֶּן לֵוִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second teaching from the same אמורא, about waiting after davening.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One should wait one hour after davening, learned from "יודו לשמך ישבו ישרים את פניך".

steps.title: A ברייתא supports both teachings
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches the same two rules, waiting before and after davening, from the same two פסוקים.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was also taught this way in a ברייתא: One who davens should wait one hour before his תפלה and one hour after it. From where do we know before? As it says, "Happy are those who dwell in Your House." From where do we know after? As it is written, "Surely the righteous will give thanks to Your name; the upright will sit before You."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says exactly what רבי יהושע בן לוי said, to support him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "תניא נמי הכי" means an earlier source, from the time of the תנאים, agrees. The ברייתא uses the same פסוק for before and the same פסוק for after, so both of רבי יהושע בן לוי's teachings are backed up.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא also teaches this (a supporting source)

phrases.english: It was also taught so in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: הַמִּתְפַּלֵּל צָרִיךְ שֶׁיִּשְׁהֶא שָׁעָה אַחַת קוֹדֶם תְּפִלָּתוֹ,
phrases.english: One who prays must wait one hour before his prayer,
and one hour after his prayer.
Before his prayer, from where do we know it?
As it is stated: "Happy are those who dwell in Your House."
After his prayer, from where do we know it?
As it is written: "Surely the righteous will give thanks to Your name,
the upright will sit before You."

steps.whatToRemember: Wait before davening comes from "אשרי יושבי ביתך". Wait after davening comes from "ישבו ישרים את פניך".
steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports steps 36 and 37 with a תנאי source.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יהושע בן לוי's two teachings about waiting before and after davening.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא that teaches both rules from the same two פסוקים.

steps.title: The early חסידים spent three hours on each תפלה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says the חסידים הראשונים waited an hour, davened for an hour, and waited another hour.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: The early חסידים would wait one hour, daven for one hour, and then wait one hour again.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא describing how the early חסידים actually davened. This sets up the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides waiting before and after, the תפלה itself took a full hour. So every תפלה took three hours from start to finish.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:

phrases.aramaic: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים הָיוּ שׁוֹהִין שָׁעָה אַחַת,
phrases.english: The early pious men would wait one hour,
and pray for one hour,
and then wait one hour again.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: חֲסִידִים הָרִאשׁוֹנִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the sources of waiting to a description of how the חסידים did it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חסידים הראשונים spent one hour waiting, one hour davening, and one hour waiting again.

steps.title: How did they have time to learn and work?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks: if they spent nine hours a day on תפלה, how did they keep up their תורה and get their work done?
steps.simpleTranslation: But since they spent nine hours a day on תפלה, how was their תורה kept, and how did their work get done?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the ברייתא: such long davening would seem to leave no time for learning or making a living.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three hours times three תפלות a day comes to nine hours. That seems to leave no room for reviewing תורה or for working. The next step answers this.

phrases.english: But since they spend
nine hours a day on prayer,
how is their Torah preserved,
and how is their work accomplished?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי מֵאַחַר שֶׁשּׁוֹהִין תֵּשַׁע שָׁעוֹת בַּיּוֹם בִּתְפִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the practice described in step 39.
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's description of the חסידים spending three hours per תפלה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nine hours a day on תפלה seems to leave no time to keep up תורה learning or to earn a living.

steps.title: Their piety protected their learning and their work
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that because the חסידים הראשונים were pious, their תורה was preserved and their work was blessed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, since they were pious, their תורה stayed with them and their work was blessed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question about how the חסידים could spend nine hours a day on תפלה. Their piety brought a special ברכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed that time spent on תפלה must be taken away from learning and from work. The answer says the normal math did not apply to them. Because of their piety, less time was enough, since their learning did not fade and their work succeeded.

keyTerms.meaning: Pious people who go beyond what is required

steps.whatToRemember: The חסידים הראשונים were not harmed by their long תפלה. Their piety kept their תורה and blessed their work.

phrases.english: Rather, because they are pious
their Torah is preserved
and their work is blessed.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִתּוֹךְ שֶׁחֲסִידִים הֵם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 40
steps.terutzResolutionType: Removes the assumed conflict: a special ברכה made up for the time spent
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Nine hours of תפלה a day would leave no time for תורה and work
steps.terutzMaskana: Their piety caused their תורה to be preserved and their work to be blessed

steps.title: Back to the משנה: don't answer even a king
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the משנה that says one should not stop praying even to answer a king's greeting.
steps.simpleTranslation: Even if the king greets him, he should not answer him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the משנה and quotes a new line from it. This sets up רב יוסף's comment in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה teaches how seriously a person must focus during תפלה: not even a king's greeting should interrupt it. The גמרא quotes this line so it can explain exactly when it applies.

keyTerms.meaning: Greets him, asks how he is doing

phrases.english: Even if the king greets him
phrases.notes: This is a line from our משנה, quoted again so the גמרא can discuss it.

phrases.english: he should not answer him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲפִילּוּ הַמֶּלֶךְ שׁוֹאֵל בִּשְׁלוֹמוֹ לֹא יְשִׁיבֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the חסידים discussion and returns to the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One does not interrupt תפלה even to answer a king's greeting

steps.title: רב יוסף: only Jewish kings, not non-Jewish kings
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף says the משנה only means Jewish kings. For a non-Jewish king, one interrupts תפלה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: They only taught this about kings of Israel. But for kings of the nations of the world, he interrupts.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף narrows the משנה's rule. It only applies to a king of ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said "the king" without saying which king. רב יוסף limits it to a Jewish king, who would understand why the person did not answer. A non-Jewish king might not understand and could react harshly, so for him the person stops and answers.
steps.confusionAlert: רב יוסף is not disagreeing with the משנה. He is explaining that its rule covers only Jewish kings.

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said:
They only taught this about kings of Israel,
but for kings of the nations of the world — he interrupts.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף, לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא לְמַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the משנה quoted in step 42
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Do not interrupt תפלה for a Jewish king, but do interrupt for a non-Jewish king

steps.title: Challenge: even when a violent person comes, you don't stop
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב יוסף with a ברייתא: even if a violent person or a carriage is coming at him, a person does not stop his תפלה. He only shortens it and moves away.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised an objection: One who is praying and saw a violent person coming toward him, or saw a carriage coming toward him, should not stop. Rather, he shortens his prayer and moves away!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב יוסף's ruling using a ברייתא. The next step gives the answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף allowed stopping for a non-Jewish king. But this ברייתא says that even in a dangerous moment, like a violent person or a carriage coming at you, you still do not stop. You only shorten your תפלה. If danger like this does not allow stopping, why should a non-Jewish king's greeting allow it?

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
One who is praying and saw a violent person coming toward him,
or saw a carriage coming toward him —
he should not stop,
but rather shortens it and moves away!
phrases.notes: וְעוֹלֶה literally means "goes up." Here it means he finishes quickly and gets out of the way.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵיתִיבִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling from step 43
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that one interrupts תפלה for a non-Jewish king
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Even real danger does not allow stopping, only shortening. So a non-Jewish king's greeting should not allow stopping either.

steps.title: Shorten if possible, stop if not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the ברייתא: it speaks of a case where he can shorten his prayer. If he cannot, he does stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. The ברייתא is talking about where it is possible to shorten, so he shortens. If not, he interrupts.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רב יוסף by saying the ברייתא only applies when the person has time to shorten his תפלה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said that even facing danger one only shortens and moves away. The גמרא limits this to a case where shortening is enough to finish in time. When there is no time, he must stop, so stopping for a non-Jewish king, as רב יוסף said, still makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not difficult. This introduces an answer.

steps.whyThisMatters: It sets the practical rule for danger during תפלה: first try to shorten, and if that is impossible, stop.

phrases.english: This is not difficult.
This is where it is possible to shorten,
phrases.notes: "This" is the ברייתא from the last step, which said to shorten and move away.

phrases.english: he should shorten.
And if not, he interrupts.
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא קַשְׁיָא, הָא דְּאֶפְשָׁר לְקַצֵּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the ברייתא in step 44.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Case limitation (אוקימתא): the ברייתא is about a case where shortening is possible.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא seemed to say one never stops תפלה, even for danger. That would contradict רב יוסף.
steps.terutzMaskana: One shortens when possible. When shortening is not possible, he stops, so רב יוסף stands.

steps.title: A pious man ignores an officer's greeting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a חסיד praying on the road. He did not answer a non-Jewish officer's greeting, and the officer waited until he finished.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: A pious man was praying on the road. An officer came and greeted him, and he did not answer. The officer waited until he finished his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story about someone who did not stop his תפלה even for a non-Jewish official. This sets up the conversation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story seems to fit poorly with רב יוסף, who said one does stop for a non-Jewish king. The pious man kept praying and risked angering a powerful officer.

phrases.english: The Sages taught: There was an incident with a certain pious man
who was praying on the road.

phrases.aramaic: בָּא הֶגְמוֹן אֶחָד וְנָתַן לוֹ שָׁלוֹם,
phrases.english: A certain officer came and greeted him,
and he did not return the greeting.
He waited for him until he finished his prayer.
phrases.notes: The officer is the one waiting.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מַעֲשֶׂה בְּחָסִיד אֶחָד שֶׁהָיָה מִתְפַּלֵּל בַּדֶּרֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story connected to the topic of stopping תפלה for a ruler.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A pious man did not interrupt his תפלה to return a non-Jewish officer's greeting.

steps.title: The officer's angry complaint
steps.stepSummary: The officer scolds the pious man. He says the תורה commands guarding one's life, and he could have killed him for ignoring the greeting.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he finished, the officer said: You fool! Doesn't your תורה say "guard yourself and guard your soul" and "guard yourselves very much"? Why didn't you return my greeting? If I had cut off your head, who would have held me responsible?
steps.whatsHappening: Inside the story, the officer attacks the pious man's behavior, using the pious man's own תורה against him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The officer argues that ignoring a powerful ruler puts one's life in danger, and the תורה forbids that. This is the challenge the pious man must now answer.

keyTerms.meaning: Empty one, a fool or good-for-nothing

phrases.english: After he finished his prayer,
he said to him: You fool!
Isn't it written in your Torah:
"Only guard yourself and guard your soul"
phrases.notes: דברים 4:9

phrases.english: and it is written: "Guard yourselves very much"?
phrases.notes: דברים 4:15

phrases.english: When I greeted you,
why didn't you return my greeting?
If I had cut off your head with a sword,

phrases.aramaic: מִי הָיָה תּוֹבֵעַ אֶת דָּמְךָ מִיָּדִי?!
phrases.english: who would have demanded your blood from my hand?!

steps.triggerLanguage: לְאַחַר שֶׁסִּייֵּם תְּפִלָּתוֹ, אָמַר לוֹ: רֵיקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story with the officer's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The pious man's choice not to stop his תפלה to answer the officer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The Torah commands guarding one's life. Ignoring a powerful ruler risks death, so the pious man acted wrongly.

steps.title: The pious man begins his explanation
steps.stepSummary: The pious man asks the officer to wait so he can calm him with words. He starts a comparison: if you stood before a human king and a friend greeted you, would you answer?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Wait, and I will appease you with words. He said: If you were standing before a flesh-and-blood king, and your friend came and greeted you, would you...
steps.whatsHappening: The pious man starts answering the officer by comparing his prayer to standing before a king. The sentence is cut off and continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He builds an argument from the officer's own world. Nobody turns away from a human king to greet a friend. The point he is heading toward is that while praying he was standing before an even greater King.

keyTerms.meaning: I will appease or calm you
A flesh-and-blood king, meaning a human king

phrases.english: He said to him: Wait for me
until I appease you with words.
